1	# CHANGE-BRIEF — Assignment 7: a sprite run cycle and a cutout-rig sword slash for Rudy
2	
3	**Revision 1 — 2026-11-12, committed before the first prompt.** Later changes are added as dated revisions at the end; this revision stays as it is.
4	
5	**How this brief was made:** Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) drafted all of it from the assignment, Chapters 10 and 11, this folder's files and the probes in `evidence/brief-probe/`. That includes the design, the tables, the rules, the predictions and the key values.
6	
7	**The assignment text.** Canvas shows Assignment 7 only as a revision note on an existing assignment. The note keeps several parts "as written" (the pin-first discipline, the state machine, the edges and re-pins) without including them. On 2026-11-12 I decided that the text it revises is the course repository's animation assignment, `assignments/08-animation-and-state.md` on `main`; I think the Canvas page was posted without that body by mistake. An earlier draft of the same note, `assignments/course-briefs/07-doing-animation.md` in the course's `walker-claude` repository (commit `48c6177ed`), bears this out: it opens by saying the first review measured the assignment "against wiring animation to player actions", the subject of that file. So this brief works to that file as changed by the note, and where the two differ, the note holds. Each requirement below comes from one of those two texts or from the chapters they assign (Chapters 10 and 11); anything else is marked as a choice of this brief.
8	
9	The choices are mine: on 2026-11-12 I chose
10	- the run cycle as the looping sprite clip;
11	- the sword slash as the committing action, on a cutout rig;
12	- Rudy's own Assignment 2 frames as the sprite source, rather than a found sheet or the course sprite set (whose path the assignment text leaves as a placeholder);
13	- to keep the slash's gameplay timing as it is.
14	
15	I reviewed the brief before committing it. The key values are a first design; the tuning loop exists to change them, with a revision here each time.
16	
17	`CLAUDE.md` is still empty. Every prompt the assignment supplies begins "Read CLAUDE.md first", so it is written before the first prompt, and it imports this file (`@CHANGE-BRIEF.md`), which makes this brief the contract the agent works to.
18	
19	This folder holds one Godot project, `game/`, copied from tag `a6`. The course's commands say `godot/`; here they say `game/`. New game files go in `game/content/rudy/` (the sheet, the rig parts, the animation library) and `game/tests/`. Design-time scripts go in `tools/` in this folder, outside the game. Frame strips go in `captures/<clip>/r<N>/`.
20	
21	## 0. The four ideas this change rests on
22	
23	1. **An animation is tracks of keys.** Every clip here is a list of tracks, each a node path and a property with keyed values. A wrong path or a wrong number still loads, so a test reads the clip back.
24	2. **One authority.** `rudy.gd` alone decides Rudy's state, as it does now. One `AnimationPlayer` alone writes what he looks like. No code sets his sprite's texture or frame, and nothing plays a clip on its own.
25	3. **Two clocks.** Gameplay runs on physics ticks; an `AnimationPlayer` runs on rendered frames unless it is told otherwise. Here it is told: both run on the physics tick, and the brief records where they could still part.
26	4. **Feel designed in frames.** The slash is designed as startup, active and recovery ticks, taken from the gameplay timing the game already has. The run is designed as a two-cell cycle with a stated seam. The keys come from those tables, and play decides whether the tables are right.
27	
28	## 1. The state
29	
30	- **Engine and renderer.** Godot 4.7.2 (`logs/checks_60fps.log:1`), GL Compatibility (`game/project.godot:16`, `:95-96`). The viewport is 1920 × 1080 with `canvas_items` stretch, in a 1280 × 720 window (`game/project.godot:25-29`).
31	- **Physics ticks per second: 60.** `game/project.godot` sets none, so the default holds (`evidence/brief-probe/logs/slash_ticks_60fps_frame.log:3`).
32	- **No animation nodes yet.** No scene or script in `game/` names `AnimationPlayer`, `AnimationTree`, `AnimatedSprite2D`, `Skeleton2D` or `Bone2D` (checked with grep on 2026-11-12).
33	- **Where Rudy's state lives.** In `game/content/rudy/rudy.gd`, as physics plus a mode:
34	  - `mode` (`rudy.gd:40-48`): `WAITING`, `PLAY`, `HURT`, `DEFEATED`, `FALLEN`, `RESPAWNING`, `CELEBRATING`;
35	  - `gear` (none or sword), `is_on_floor()`, `velocity`, and the swing clock `_slash_clock` (`rudy.gd:92`, `:116-117`).
36	
37	  Every physics tick, `_physics_process` (`rudy.gd:198-234`) moves him, runs `_swing()` and then `_pick_pose()` (`rudy.gd:285-311`). That is a priority list, like `visual_animation()` in walker-jumpman-clawd (Chapter 11), and it returns a pose's asset ID. `_look.show_pose(pose)` (`rudy.gd:234`) then sets the Sprite's texture to that pose's PNG (`game/content/rudy/rudy_look.gd:39-46`). There are no transitions and no cross-fades: every change is a cut on the tick its condition changes.
38	- **The run today.** `_run_clock` (`rudy.gd:84`) counts up while he runs on the floor. With `run_frame_time` 0.125 s (`rudy.gd:61`) he shows `RUN-A`, then `RUN-B`, and so on (`rudy.gd:306-309`). The clock is reset in the air and when he stands (`rudy.gd:299`, `:310`). It is neither reset nor advanced during a swing (`rudy.gd:295-296`), so a run resumes its phase after a slash.
39	- **The slash today, measured** (`evidence/brief-probe/logs/slash_ticks_60fps_frame.log:4-21`). Tick 0 is the tick the press is read:
40	
41	  | Ticks | Pose | Hitbox | Why |
42	  |---|---|---|---|
43	  | 0–1 | `CHAR-SWORD-SLASH` | dead | the clock is below `slash_live_from` 0.03 s when `_swing()` reads it (`rudy.gd:67`, `:241`) |
44	  | 2–10 | `CHAR-SWORD-SLASH` | **live**, 9 ticks (0.15 s) | 2/60 s to 10/60 s lie within 0.03–0.18 s (`rudy.gd:67-68`) |
45	  | 11–16 | `CHAR-SWORD-SLASH` | dead | past `slash_live_to` |
46	  | 17 | `CHAR-SWORD-IDLE` | dead | the clock reaches `slash_time` 0.3 s on this tick's increment, and the swing ends on the same tick (`rudy.gd:248-251`) |
47	
48	  So the swing is on screen for **17 ticks (0.283 s), not 18.** A press is ignored while a swing is under way (`rudy.gd:223`), including on tick 17, because the press is read before `_swing()` ends the swing. The earliest next swing is read on tick 18.
49	- **What cancels a swing.** A hit (`rudy.gd:143`), a fall out of the level (`rudy.gd:168`), a respawn (`rudy.gd:182`) and the teleport circle (`rudy.gd:195`). Jumping and moving do not. Turning does not either: `facing` changes mid-swing (`rudy.gd:204-208`), so the hitbox and the look flip with him (`rudy.gd:231`, `:240`).
50	- **Rudy's frames** (`game/content/rudy/frames/frames.json`):
51	  - 16 PNGs, each on a 410 × 386 canvas, with the body origin (his soles, on the torso line) at texture pixel (205, 370);
52	  - stored at density 2: 2 texture px per game px. The Sprite draws them at scale 0.5, `centered` off, offset (−205, −370) (`game/content/rudy/rudy.tscn:27-32`);
53	  - with the 4 px outline material (`game/systems/art/outline.gdshader`, width 8 texture px) and linear mipmap filtering.
54	
55	  Every frame keeps at least 16 texture px of transparent margin on each side (`evidence/brief-probe/logs/frame_margins.log:17`), so neither the outline nor a mipmap reaches a neighbouring cell when they share a sheet.
56	- **What the existing tests read of his look** (`game/tests/checks.gd`):
57	  - `Rudy.pose` as an asset ID in many checks, including the run's `RUN-A`/`RUN-B` trail (`checks.gd:172-173`), the air poses (`:197-198`, `:301`, `:310`) and the slash (`:727-733`);
58	  - `RudyLook.FRAMES` and `RudyLook.frame()`, compared on every tick (`checks.gd:129-131`);
59	  - the frames manifest, the Sprite's offset, scale and centring, and its filter and outline (`checks.gd:848-878`);
60	  - that every pose but the block showed its own frame (`checks.gd:879-886`).
61	
62	  These existing checks are tied to today's texture swap. They are earlier tests, so they keep passing unchanged (section 5).
63	- **How the existing tests press keys.** `checks.gd` uses `Input.action_press` (`checks.gd:167` and on). New tests use `Input.parse_input_event` with the project's physical keys: D (move right), A (move left), Space (jump), J (slash) (`game/project.godot:33-68`). `action_press` never reaches `_input` or `_unhandled_input`; `parse_input_event` goes the way a real key does. A probe press of J through `parse_input_event` was read as `slash` on the next physics tick (`evidence/brief-probe/logs/slash_ticks_60fps_frame.log:4`).
64	
65	## 2. The animation set
66	
67	The assignment's minimum is two clips, one sprite and one rig. One must loop and one must be a committing action, and at least one is driven by the player's state machine. Here both are Rudy's, and both are driven by his state machine.
68	
69	| Clip | Role | Route | Source | Driven by |
70	|---|---|---|---|---|
71	| `run`, `sword_run` | **The looping sprite clip** | `Sprite2D` with an `AnimationPlayer` frame track | Rudy's run frames, packed into a sheet | `rudy.gd`'s state |
72	| `slash` | **The committing action, on a rig** | Cutout rig keyed as resource text | Parts cut from `CHAR-SWORD-SLASH.png` | `rudy.gd`'s state |
73	
74	The state machine needs more states than these two clips (section 3). Each other state gets a **one-key clip** on the same `AnimationPlayer`, keying the Sprite's frame to that pose's cell. Those are not part of the two-clip set: they replace today's texture swap, so that one player draws everything.
75	
76	All clips live in one `AnimationLibrary`, `game/content/rudy/rudy_animations.tres`, written as resource text so that every key is readable in a diff. The `AnimationPlayer` is a child of `Rudy/Look`, with `root_node` left at `..` (its parent, `Look`; `evidence/brief-probe/logs/godot3_names_resource.log:5`). Its settings:
77	- `callback_mode_process` physics (section 4);
78	- `autoplay` empty;
79	- `speed_scale` 1.0.
80	
81	### 2.1 Clip 1 — the run cycle (sprite, loops)
82	
83	**Route:** `Sprite2D` with an `AnimationPlayer` frame track. The sheet is sliced with `hframes` and `vframes`, and the clip keys `frame`.
84	
85	**Source and terms.** Rudy's frames were generated in Assignment 2 with the Gemini app's image generation, under Google's Terms of Service and Generative AI Additional Terms (`../assignment-2/SOURCES.md:33`), and follow Assignment 2's rules for generated art.
86	- The accepted originals are `../assignment-2/generated/accepted/CHAR-*.jpg`.
87	- `../assignment-2/design/tools/matte_sprites.py` made the game frames in `game/content/rudy/frames/` from them.
88	
89	They have been in this repository, which is public, since Assignment 2 (the `shuai-z/assignment-2` branch), and they appear in the films of Assignments 2, 5 and 6. The editable sources are those originals and the frames themselves. Both are committed and stay unedited. No found sheet and no third-party licence is involved. SOURCES.md records this again for Assignment 7.
90	
91	**The sheet** is `game/content/rudy/sheet/rudy_sheet.png`, made by `tools/pack_rudy_sheet.py` from the 16 game frames, with no scaling and no edits:
92	- **cell** 410 × 386 px, no padding;
93	- **grid** 4 columns × 4 rows (`hframes` 4, `vframes` 4), 1640 × 1544 px;
94	- **frame order** row by row, in `frames.json` order:
95	
96	| Cell | Pose | Cell | Pose | Cell | Pose | Cell | Pose |
97	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
98	| 0 | `CHAR-IDLE` | 4 | `CHAR-FALL` | 8 | `CHAR-CELEBRATE` | 12 | `CHAR-SWORD-RUN-A` |
99	| 1 | `CHAR-RUN-A` | 5 | `CHAR-HURT` | 9 | `CHAR-SWORD-IDLE` | 13 | `CHAR-SWORD-RUN-B` |
100	| 2 | `CHAR-RUN-B` | 6 | `CHAR-DEFEAT` | 10 | `CHAR-SWORD-SLASH` | 14 | `CHAR-SWORD-RISE` |
101	| 3 | `CHAR-RISE` | 7 | `CHAR-RESPAWN` | 11 | `CHAR-SWORD-BLOCK` | 15 | `CHAR-SWORD-FALL` |
102	
103	- **The last cell is 15.** A frame key of 16 or more points outside the sheet.
104	- **The packing script asserts** that each cell equals its source PNG pixel for pixel, and prints the sheet's SHA-256.
105	- **The sheet imports with mipmaps** (`mipmaps/generate=true`), like the frames (`game/content/rudy/frames/CHAR-IDLE.png.import`).
106	- **The Sprite keeps** its offset (−205, −370), its scale 0.5, `centered` off, the outline material and the filter it inherits from `Look`. With `hframes` and `vframes` set, each cell is drawn where its frame was drawn.
107	
108	**Registration.** Every frame puts the body origin at texture pixel (205, 370) (`frames.json`), so the body origin sits at the same place in every cell. The check is the frame strip: his soles stay on the walk line in every cell, and the run's two cells do not jump against each other.
109	
110	**The cycle:**
111	
112	| | `run` | `sword_run` |
113	|---|---|---|
114	| Cells | 1 (`RUN-A`) at 0.0 s, 2 (`RUN-B`) at 0.125 s | 12 (`SWORD-RUN-A`) at 0.0 s, 13 (`SWORD-RUN-B`) at 0.125 s |
115	| Cell rate | 8 cells/s: 0.125 s per cell, today's `run_frame_time` (`rudy.gd:61`) | the same |
116	| `length` | 0.25 s | 0.25 s |
117	| Update mode | `UPDATE_DISCRETE` | `UPDATE_DISCRETE` |
118	| `loop_mode` | `LOOP_LINEAR` | `LOOP_LINEAR` |
119	
120	- **The seam rule for a frame track.** There is no duplicate across the wrap: the last key is B and the first is A. The gap from the last key to `length` (0.25 − 0.125) equals the key interval (0.125).
121	- **Ticks per cell.** At 60 ticks/s a cell lasts 7.5 ticks, so cells alternate 8 and 7 ticks (`evidence/brief-probe/logs/anim_run_discrete_60fps.log:8-31`), much as today's clock does.
122	- **Restart.** The run plays from `RUN-A` whenever he enters it from any other state. Today's run restarts from A after standing and after the air, but resumes its phase after a slash (section 1). The new clip restarts from A after a slash too. **That is the one intended change to the run's timing.** The pin records today's resume, and the re-pin records the restart, after I have played it.
123	- **One source for the timing.** `run_frame_time` and `_run_clock` leave `rudy.gd`; the clip's keys become the only source of the run's timing. No existing test reads either of them.
124	
125	### 2.2 Clip 2 — the slash (cutout rig, commits)
126	
127	**Route:** cutout rig keyed as resource text. The agent writes the keys directly in `rudy_animations.tres`.
128	
129	**Rig source.** `tools/cut_slash_rig.py` cuts parts from `game/content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-SLASH.png`, whose provenance is that of section 2.1. The parts go in `game/content/rudy/rig/`, each on the same 410 × 386 canvas with the same origin, so that at rest they register exactly on the original frame:
130	- `slash_body.png`: the frame without the blade and without the translucent arc. Where the arc crosses the robe and the shield, the script repairs the pixels from the surrounding robe and shield.
131	- `slash_blade.png`: the blade and crossguard, from the fist outwards.
132	- `slash_arc.png`: the translucent arc alone.
133	
134	The script measures and prints the grip point (the centre of the fist around the hilt, near texture pixel (258, 165)). It checks that the three parts, composited at rest, equal the original frame except inside the repaired band, and it prints the size of that band. The parts are a derivative of my own generated art. The original frame stays as it is, and the script and the parts are committed as the rig's editable source.
135	
136	**Rig nodes**, all under `Rudy/Look`, so they flip with `facing` and flash with the invulnerability fade as the Sprite does:
137	
138	```text
139	Look
140	├── Sprite            Sprite2D, the sheet; hidden during the slash
141	├── SlashRig          Node2D, visible only during the slash
142	│   └── Lean          Node2D, pivot at his soles (0, 0); keyed position and rotation_degrees
143	│       ├── Grip      Node2D, pivot at the grip point; keyed rotation_degrees
144	│       │   └── Blade Sprite2D, slash_blade.png, drawn BEHIND Body
145	│       ├── Body      Sprite2D, slash_body.png
146	│       └── Arc       Sprite2D, slash_arc.png; keyed modulate:a; no outline material
147	└── AnimationPlayer
148	```
149	
150	- **Draw order.** Blade comes before Body in the tree, so the fist covers the hilt and the blade's outline does not cross his hand.
151	- **Materials.** Body and Blade use the outline material; Arc does not, as the faint trail has none today (`outline.gdshader:8-9`).
152	- **Sprite settings.** Every part keeps the Sprite's offset and scale, so its canvas origin sits on Rudy's origin. Blade is offset from the Grip pivot so that, at Grip 0°, it sits where it was drawn.
153	
154	**The phase table.** Frames are physics ticks at 60 per second, and tick 0 is the press tick. This is today's gameplay timing (section 1), which this change keeps. The clip's frame rate is 60, so a key's time is its tick divided by 60. The clip starts on tick 0, because the player is always playing a state clip when the slash starts (section 4).
155	
156	| Phase | Ticks | Clip time | Hitbox (gameplay, unchanged) | What the rig does |
157	|---|---|---|---|---|
158	| **Startup** | 0–1 | 0 – 2/60 s | dead | The blade is raised back over his shoulder (Grip −70° → −60°) and his weight sits back (Lean −2°). Two ticks: at 30 fps one rendered frame, so the wind-up reads as one held pose |
159	| **Active** | 2–10 | 2/60 – 11/60 s | **live** | The blade sweeps forward and down, accelerating: Grip −60° → 0° (the drawn angle) at tick 5 → +45° at tick 11. He leans into it (Lean +3°, x +6 px by tick 5). The arc appears at tick 2 (α 0 → 1 by tick 4) and fades by tick 11 |
160	| **Recovery** | 11–16 | 11/60 – 17/60 s | dead | The blade settles back: Grip +45° → +15°, decelerating. Lean returns to 0°, x 0 |
161	| **End** | 17 | 17/60 s | the swing ends (`rudy.gd:250-251`) | The clip's `length` is 17/60 s (0.2833 s). The state leaves `slash` on this tick, a cut to the sword form's idle, run or air pose |
162	
163	**Keys at every phase boundary.** Key times are 0, 2/60, 5/60, 11/60 and 17/60 s, on these tracks:
164	
165	| Track | 0 | 2/60 | 5/60 | 11/60 | 17/60 | Transitions |
166	|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
167	| `Look/Sprite:visible` (discrete) | false | | | | | |
168	| `Look/SlashRig:visible` (discrete) | true | | | | | |
169	| `Look/SlashRig/Lean/Grip:rotation_degrees` | −70 | −60 | 0 | 45 | 15 | ease-in (accelerating) into the active keys; ease-out (settling) from 11/60 |
170	| `Look/SlashRig/Lean:rotation_degrees` | −2 | −2 | 3 | 3 | 0 | ease-out from 11/60 |
171	| `Look/SlashRig/Lean:position` | (0, 0) | (0, 0) | (6, 0) | (6, 0) | (0, 0) | ease-out from 11/60 |
172	| `Look/SlashRig/Lean/Arc:modulate:a` | 0 | 0 | 1 (at 4/60) | 0 | 0 | linear |
173	
174	- **Visibility.** Every other state clip keys `Sprite:visible` true and `SlashRig:visible` false at time 0, so leaving the slash on any tick shows the Sprite again.
175	- **Loop and positive angles.** `loop_mode` is `LOOP_NONE`. Positive angles turn clockwise on screen (y points down), so +45° points the blade forward and down.
176	- **The agent's key table.** The agent lists every key time beside the tick it comes from.
177	
178	**Interrupts by phase.** These are unchanged gameplay rules, and the clip follows them:
179	
180	| Event | Startup | Active | Recovery |
181	|---|---|---|---|
182	| Slash pressed again | ignored: no new swing, the clip is not restarted | ignored | ignored, including on tick 17 |
183	| Jump pressed on the floor | he jumps; the swing plays on in the air | the same | the same |
184	| Move or turn | he moves or turns; the rig flips with `Look` on the tick he turns | the same | the same |
185	| A hit (with the sword, it always knocks the sword away) | the swing ends on that tick: hurt clip, Sprite shown, rig hidden, hitbox dead | the same | the same |
186	| Fall out, respawn, teleport circle | the swing ends on that tick | the same | the same |
187	| Pause | the clip freezes with the tree; it goes on from the same point on resume | the same | the same |
188	
189	## 3. The state machine
190	
191	**Wiring: the existing priority list stays the single authority.** `rudy.gd` keeps choosing his state every physics tick with today's priorities, but the choice is now a clip name, not an asset ID. `RudyLook` plays that clip when it differs from the one playing. I chose this over an `AnimationTree`:
192	- **One authority.** The selector already is it. A tree with its own transitions would be a second machine that could disagree with it (Chapter 11).
193	- **No sampling gap.** The selector runs on every physics tick, so the gap Chapter 11 found between physics ticks and tree updates cannot open.
194	- **Nothing to blend.** There is nothing to cross-fade between whole frames.
195	
196	Its weakness is the one Chapter 11 names for walker-jumpman-clawd: every change is a cut.
197	
198	**The restart rule.** `play()` with the name already playing does not restart it (`evidence/brief-probe/logs/anim_clock_physics_60fps.log:13-14`). A new swing always follows at least one tick of another state (section 1), but `RudyLook` still starts every new swing with `play("slash")` and `seek(0.0, true)`, so the rule never rests on that gap.
199	
200	**What keeps its meaning,** so that the existing checks pass unchanged:
201	- `Rudy.pose` is the asset ID of the pose on screen, read after the tick's animation update: the cell's pose while the Sprite shows, and `CHAR-SWORD-SLASH` while the rig shows.
202	- `RudyLook.FRAMES` maps every asset ID to its original PNG.
203	- `RudyLook.frame()` returns the original PNG of the pose on screen. During the slash that is `CHAR-SWORD-SLASH.png`, the frame the rig is cut from.
204	
205	**The states.** Higher in the table wins, as in `_pick_pose()` today:
206	
207	| # | State (clip) | Shows | Entered when | Loops | Cross-fade |
208	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
209	| 1 | `celebrate` | cell 8 | `mode` is `CELEBRATING`: on the teleport circle (`rudy.gd:193-195`) | one key, `LOOP_LINEAR` | none, a cut |
210	| 2 | `respawn` | cell 7 | `mode` is `RESPAWNING`, for `respawn_time` 0.7 s (`rudy.gd:177-190`) | one key, linear | cut |
211	| 3 | `defeat` | cell 6 | `mode` is `DEFEATED`: a hit took his last heart (`rudy.gd:147`) | one key, linear | cut |
212	| 4 | `hurt` | cell 5 | `mode` is `HURT`, for `hurt_time` 0.35 s (`rudy.gd:151`) | one key, linear | cut |
213	| 5 | `slash` | the rig | `is_slashing()`: a fresh slash press with the sword, and no swing under way (`rudy.gd:223-226`) | `LOOP_NONE` | cut |
214	| 6 | `rise` / `sword_rise` | cell 3 / 14 | off the floor, and not in the falling pose's case below | one key, linear | cut |
215	| 7 | `fall` / `sword_fall` | cell 4 / 15 | off the floor, falling (`velocity.y` ≥ 0), and moving sideways when the fall began (`rudy.gd:298-304`) | one key, linear | cut |
216	| 8 | `run` / `sword_run` | cells 1–2 / 12–13 | on the floor, `absf(velocity.x)` > 1 (`rudy.gd:306-309`) | `LOOP_LINEAR` | cut |
217	| 9 | `idle` / `sword_idle` | cell 0 / 9 | otherwise, including `WAITING` on the title | one key, linear | cut |
218	
219	- **Air poses.** `FALLEN` (below a cliff) shows the air states by rule 6 or 7.
220	- **Forms.** States 6 to 9 use the sword form's clip while `gear` is the sword.
221	- **Single-key clips loop.** They loop so that the player never stops: a `play()` on a stopped player shows its first key one tick late (`evidence/brief-probe/logs/anim_clock_physics_60fps.log:7-8`, against `:26-28`).
222	- **Cuts everywhere.** Whole frames cannot cross-fade, and the rig appears and disappears on a tick, so every transition is a cut on the tick its condition changes, as today.
223	
224	**Every transition out of every state**, written before reading the agent's list:
225	
226	| From | To | When |
227	|---|---|---|
228	| `idle` | `run` | a direction is held: at once if he faces it, after `turn_hold_time` 0.12 s if it turns him (`rudy.gd:204-215`) |
229	| | `rise` | a fresh jump press on the floor (`rudy.gd:219-222`) |
230	| | `slash` | a fresh slash press with the sword |
231	| | `hurt` / `defeat` | a hit; `defeat` if it took his last heart (only without the sword) |
232	| | `celebrate` | he reaches the teleport circle |

255	## 4. Two clocks
256	
257	- **Gameplay** runs in `rudy.gd`'s `_physics_process`, 60 ticks/s, and the hitbox stays there: `_swing()` reads `_slash_clock` (`rudy.gd:239-251`). **No animation key decides a gameplay fact.** The clip only draws; the hitbox, the slash sound (`rudy.gd:226`) and Effect A's sparks (which watch `SwordHitbox/Shape.disabled`, `game/effects/effects_driver.gd`) stay as they are.
258	- **The `AnimationPlayer`'s `callback_mode_process` is physics (0), set in the scene,** not the default idle (1) (`evidence/brief-probe/logs/anim_clock_physics_60fps.log:3`). In physics mode the clip time is (ticks since `play()`)/60 at 60 fps and at 30 fps alike (`anim_clock_physics_30fps.log:9-13`). In idle mode at 30 fps it advanced once per rendered frame, in uneven steps (0, 0.0292, 0.0592 s; `anim_clock_idle_30fps.log:7-13`): a second clock that would let the rig's active keys drift off the live ticks.
259	- **Order within a tick.** The player is a child of `Look`, which is a child of `Rudy`, and in the probe a child's physics processing ran after its host's `_physics_process` on the same tick. So a `play()` from `rudy.gd` on tick 0 shows the clip's first key on tick 0, provided the player was already playing (`anim_clock_physics_60fps.log:27-28`).
260	- **Method callbacks** stay deferred (the default, 0). No clip has a method track, so nothing depends on when a method key runs.
261	- **No `AnimatedSprite2D`** is used, so no second sprite clock exists.
262	- **The rendered frame.** Tests run at `--fixed-fps 60`: one tick per frame. Movie Maker captures run at 30 fps: two ticks per frame, and each PNG shows the state after the frame's second tick.

444	## 12. How the agent sessions run
445	
446	The rules below are the ones the assignment states; the source of each is in brackets.
447	
448	- **One step per prompt.** One bounded step per prompt and one commit per verified step [course text, "Pin first, then change"]. Each prompt runs as its own Claude Code session with stream-JSON output, as in Chapter 10's command.
449	- **Git is read-only for the agent** (status, diff, log, show) [revision note, "Keep read-only git"].
450	- **The result event.** A session counts only if its stream-JSON ends with a `result` event whose subtype is `success` [revision note, "the result-event check"]. A session that ends any other way, at a usage limit or a turn limit, is **interrupted**.
451	- **Resuming** [revision note, "Add a rule for resuming interrupted sessions"]. An interrupted session's uncommitted work is not built on. I inspect its diff and rerun its checks through the wrapper. Then either I commit it as its own verified step, or I discard it with `git restore` and `git clean` limited to the files it touched. Only then does a new session start, with a prompt that says what the old one left.

459	- The goblins keep their code-picked frames (`goblin.gd:112-118`). `CHAR-SWORD-BLOCK` stays unused, as today (`checks.gd:879-882`).

# CHANGE-BRIEF — Assignment 7: a sprite run cycle and a cutout-rig sword slash for Rudy

**Revision 1 — 2026-11-12, committed before the first prompt.** Later changes are added as dated revisions at the end; this revision stays as it is.

**How this brief was made:** Claude Code (Claude Opus 5.5) drafted all of it from the assignment, Chapters 10 and 11, this folder's files and the probes in `evidence/brief-probe/`. That includes the design, the tables, the rules, the predictions and the key values.

**The assignment text.** Canvas shows Assignment 7 only as a revision note on an existing assignment. The note keeps several parts "as written" (the pin-first discipline, the state machine, the edges and re-pins) without including them. On 2026-11-12 I decided that the text it revises is the course repository's animation assignment, `assignments/08-animation-and-state.md` on `main`; I think the Canvas page was posted without that body by mistake. An earlier draft of the same note, `assignments/course-briefs/07-doing-animation.md` in the course's `walker-claude` repository (commit `48c6177ed`), bears this out: it opens by saying the first review measured the assignment "against wiring animation to player actions", the subject of that file. So this brief works to that file as changed by the note, and where the two differ, the note holds. Each requirement below comes from one of those two texts or from the chapters they assign (Chapters 10 and 11); anything else is marked as a choice of this brief.

The choices are mine: on 2026-11-12 I chose
- the run cycle as the looping sprite clip;
- the sword slash as the committing action, on a cutout rig;
- Rudy's own Assignment 2 frames as the sprite source, rather than a found sheet or the course sprite set (whose path the assignment text leaves as a placeholder);
- to keep the slash's gameplay timing as it is.

I reviewed the brief before committing it. The key values are a first design; the tuning loop exists to change them, with a revision here each time.

`CLAUDE.md` is still empty. Every prompt the assignment supplies begins "Read CLAUDE.md first", so it is written before the first prompt, and it imports this file (`@CHANGE-BRIEF.md`), which makes this brief the contract the agent works to.

This folder holds one Godot project, `game/`, copied from tag `a6`. The course's commands say `godot/`; here they say `game/`. New game files go in `game/content/rudy/` (the sheet, the rig parts, the animation library) and `game/tests/`. Design-time scripts go in `tools/` in this folder, outside the game. Frame strips go in `captures/<clip>/r<N>/`.

## 0. The four ideas this change rests on

1. **An animation is tracks of keys.** Every clip here is a list of tracks, each a node path and a property with keyed values. A wrong path or a wrong number still loads, so a test reads the clip back.
2. **One authority.** `rudy.gd` alone decides Rudy's state, as it does now. One `AnimationPlayer` alone writes what he looks like. No code sets his sprite's texture or frame, and nothing plays a clip on its own.
3. **Two clocks.** Gameplay runs on physics ticks; an `AnimationPlayer` runs on rendered frames unless it is told otherwise. Here it is told: both run on the physics tick, and the brief records where they could still part.
4. **Feel designed in frames.** The slash is designed as startup, active and recovery ticks, taken from the gameplay timing the game already has. The run is designed as a two-cell cycle with a stated seam. The keys come from those tables, and play decides whether the tables are right.

## 1. The state

- **Engine and renderer.** Godot 4.7.2 (`logs/checks_60fps.log:1`), GL Compatibility (`game/project.godot:16`, `:95-96`). The viewport is 1920 × 1080 with `canvas_items` stretch, in a 1280 × 720 window (`game/project.godot:25-29`).
- **Physics ticks per second: 60.** `game/project.godot` sets none, so the default holds (`evidence/brief-probe/logs/slash_ticks_60fps_frame.log:3`).
- **No animation nodes yet.** No scene or script in `game/` names `AnimationPlayer`, `AnimationTree`, `AnimatedSprite2D`, `Skeleton2D` or `Bone2D` (checked with grep on 2026-11-12).
- **Where Rudy's state lives.** In `game/content/rudy/rudy.gd`, as physics plus a mode:
  - `mode` (`rudy.gd:40-48`): `WAITING`, `PLAY`, `HURT`, `DEFEATED`, `FALLEN`, `RESPAWNING`, `CELEBRATING`;
  - `gear` (none or sword), `is_on_floor()`, `velocity`, and the swing clock `_slash_clock` (`rudy.gd:92`, `:116-117`).

  Every physics tick, `_physics_process` (`rudy.gd:198-234`) moves him, runs `_swing()` and then `_pick_pose()` (`rudy.gd:285-311`). That is a priority list, like `visual_animation()` in walker-jumpman-clawd (Chapter 11), and it returns a pose's asset ID. `_look.show_pose(pose)` (`rudy.gd:234`) then sets the Sprite's texture to that pose's PNG (`game/content/rudy/rudy_look.gd:39-46`). There are no transitions and no cross-fades: every change is a cut on the tick its condition changes.
- **The run today.** `_run_clock` (`rudy.gd:84`) counts up while he runs on the floor. With `run_frame_time` 0.125 s (`rudy.gd:61`) he shows `RUN-A`, then `RUN-B`, and so on (`rudy.gd:306-309`). The clock is reset in the air and when he stands (`rudy.gd:299`, `:310`). It is neither reset nor advanced during a swing (`rudy.gd:295-296`), so a run resumes its phase after a slash.
- **The slash today, measured** (`evidence/brief-probe/logs/slash_ticks_60fps_frame.log:4-21`). Tick 0 is the tick the press is read:

  | Ticks | Pose | Hitbox | Why |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | 0–1 | `CHAR-SWORD-SLASH` | dead | the clock is below `slash_live_from` 0.03 s when `_swing()` reads it (`rudy.gd:67`, `:241`) |
  | 2–10 | `CHAR-SWORD-SLASH` | **live**, 9 ticks (0.15 s) | 2/60 s to 10/60 s lie within 0.03–0.18 s (`rudy.gd:67-68`) |
  | 11–16 | `CHAR-SWORD-SLASH` | dead | past `slash_live_to` |
  | 17 | `CHAR-SWORD-IDLE` | dead | the clock reaches `slash_time` 0.3 s on this tick's increment, and the swing ends on the same tick (`rudy.gd:248-251`) |

  So the swing is on screen for **17 ticks (0.283 s), not 18.** A press is ignored while a swing is under way (`rudy.gd:223`), including on tick 17, because the press is read before `_swing()` ends the swing. The earliest next swing is read on tick 18.
- **What cancels a swing.** A hit (`rudy.gd:143`), a fall out of the level (`rudy.gd:168`), a respawn (`rudy.gd:182`) and the teleport circle (`rudy.gd:195`). Jumping and moving do not. Turning does not either: `facing` changes mid-swing (`rudy.gd:204-208`), so the hitbox and the look flip with him (`rudy.gd:231`, `:240`).
- **Rudy's frames** (`game/content/rudy/frames/frames.json`):
  - 16 PNGs, each on a 410 × 386 canvas, with the body origin (his soles, on the torso line) at texture pixel (205, 370);
  - stored at density 2: 2 texture px per game px. The Sprite draws them at scale 0.5, `centered` off, offset (−205, −370) (`game/content/rudy/rudy.tscn:27-32`);
  - with the 4 px outline material (`game/systems/art/outline.gdshader`, width 8 texture px) and linear mipmap filtering.

  Every frame keeps at least 16 texture px of transparent margin on each side (`evidence/brief-probe/logs/frame_margins.log:17`), so neither the outline nor a mipmap reaches a neighbouring cell when they share a sheet.
- **What the existing tests read of his look** (`game/tests/checks.gd`):
  - `Rudy.pose` as an asset ID in many checks, including the run's `RUN-A`/`RUN-B` trail (`checks.gd:172-173`), the air poses (`:197-198`, `:301`, `:310`) and the slash (`:727-733`);
  - `RudyLook.FRAMES` and `RudyLook.frame()`, compared on every tick (`checks.gd:129-131`);
  - the frames manifest, the Sprite's offset, scale and centring, and its filter and outline (`checks.gd:848-878`);
  - that every pose but the block showed its own frame (`checks.gd:879-886`).

  These existing checks are tied to today's texture swap. They are earlier tests, so they keep passing unchanged (section 5).
- **How the existing tests press keys.** `checks.gd` uses `Input.action_press` (`checks.gd:167` and on). New tests use `Input.parse_input_event` with the project's physical keys: D (move right), A (move left), Space (jump), J (slash) (`game/project.godot:33-68`). `action_press` never reaches `_input` or `_unhandled_input`; `parse_input_event` goes the way a real key does. A probe press of J through `parse_input_event` was read as `slash` on the next physics tick (`evidence/brief-probe/logs/slash_ticks_60fps_frame.log:4`).

## 2. The animation set

The assignment's minimum is two clips, one sprite and one rig. One must loop and one must be a committing action, and at least one is driven by the player's state machine. Here both are Rudy's, and both are driven by his state machine.

| Clip | Role | Route | Source | Driven by |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `run`, `sword_run` | **The looping sprite clip** | `Sprite2D` with an `AnimationPlayer` frame track | Rudy's run frames, packed into a sheet | `rudy.gd`'s state |
| `slash` | **The committing action, on a rig** | Cutout rig keyed as resource text | Parts cut from `CHAR-SWORD-SLASH.png` | `rudy.gd`'s state |

The state machine needs more states than these two clips (section 3). Each other state gets a **one-key clip** on the same `AnimationPlayer`, keying the Sprite's frame to that pose's cell. Those are not part of the two-clip set: they replace today's texture swap, so that one player draws everything.

All clips live in one `AnimationLibrary`, `game/content/rudy/rudy_animations.tres`, written as resource text so that every key is readable in a diff. The `AnimationPlayer` is a child of `Rudy/Look`, with `root_node` left at `..` (its parent, `Look`; `evidence/brief-probe/logs/godot3_names_resource.log:5`). Its settings:
- `callback_mode_process` physics (section 4);
- `autoplay` empty;
- `speed_scale` 1.0.

### 2.1 Clip 1 — the run cycle (sprite, loops)

**Route:** `Sprite2D` with an `AnimationPlayer` frame track. The sheet is sliced with `hframes` and `vframes`, and the clip keys `frame`.

**Source and terms.** Rudy's frames were generated in Assignment 2 with the Gemini app's image generation, under Google's Terms of Service and Generative AI Additional Terms (`../assignment-2/SOURCES.md:33`), and follow Assignment 2's rules for generated art.
- The accepted originals are `../assignment-2/generated/accepted/CHAR-*.jpg`.
- `../assignment-2/design/tools/matte_sprites.py` made the game frames in `game/content/rudy/frames/` from them.

They have been in this repository, which is public, since Assignment 2 (the `shuai-z/assignment-2` branch), and they appear in the films of Assignments 2, 5 and 6. The editable sources are those originals and the frames themselves. Both are committed and stay unedited. No found sheet and no third-party licence is involved. SOURCES.md records this again for Assignment 7.

**The sheet** is `game/content/rudy/sheet/rudy_sheet.png`, made by `tools/pack_rudy_sheet.py` from the 16 game frames, with no scaling and no edits:
- **cell** 410 × 386 px, no padding;
- **grid** 4 columns × 4 rows (`hframes` 4, `vframes` 4), 1640 × 1544 px;
- **frame order** row by row, in `frames.json` order:

| Cell | Pose | Cell | Pose | Cell | Pose | Cell | Pose |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `CHAR-IDLE` | 4 | `CHAR-FALL` | 8 | `CHAR-CELEBRATE` | 12 | `CHAR-SWORD-RUN-A` |
| 1 | `CHAR-RUN-A` | 5 | `CHAR-HURT` | 9 | `CHAR-SWORD-IDLE` | 13 | `CHAR-SWORD-RUN-B` |
| 2 | `CHAR-RUN-B` | 6 | `CHAR-DEFEAT` | 10 | `CHAR-SWORD-SLASH` | 14 | `CHAR-SWORD-RISE` |
| 3 | `CHAR-RISE` | 7 | `CHAR-RESPAWN` | 11 | `CHAR-SWORD-BLOCK` | 15 | `CHAR-SWORD-FALL` |

- **The last cell is 15.** A frame key of 16 or more points outside the sheet.
- **The packing script asserts** that each cell equals its source PNG pixel for pixel, and prints the sheet's SHA-256.
- **The sheet imports with mipmaps** (`mipmaps/generate=true`), like the frames (`game/content/rudy/frames/CHAR-IDLE.png.import`).
- **The Sprite keeps** its offset (−205, −370), its scale 0.5, `centered` off, the outline material and the filter it inherits from `Look`. With `hframes` and `vframes` set, each cell is drawn where its frame was drawn.

**Registration.** Every frame puts the body origin at texture pixel (205, 370) (`frames.json`), so the body origin sits at the same place in every cell. The check is the frame strip: his soles stay on the walk line in every cell, and the run's two cells do not jump against each other.

**The cycle:**

| | `run` | `sword_run` |
|---|---|---|
| Cells | 1 (`RUN-A`) at 0.0 s, 2 (`RUN-B`) at 0.125 s | 12 (`SWORD-RUN-A`) at 0.0 s, 13 (`SWORD-RUN-B`) at 0.125 s |
| Cell rate | 8 cells/s: 0.125 s per cell, today's `run_frame_time` (`rudy.gd:61`) | the same |
| `length` | 0.25 s | 0.25 s |
| Update mode | `UPDATE_DISCRETE` | `UPDATE_DISCRETE` |
| `loop_mode` | `LOOP_LINEAR` | `LOOP_LINEAR` |

- **The seam rule for a frame track.** There is no duplicate across the wrap: the last key is B and the first is A. The gap from the last key to `length` (0.25 − 0.125) equals the key interval (0.125).
- **Ticks per cell.** At 60 ticks/s a cell lasts 7.5 ticks, so cells alternate 8 and 7 ticks (`evidence/brief-probe/logs/anim_run_discrete_60fps.log:8-31`), much as today's clock does.
- **Restart.** The run plays from `RUN-A` whenever he enters it from any other state. Today's run restarts from A after standing and after the air, but resumes its phase after a slash (section 1). The new clip restarts from A after a slash too. **That is the one intended change to the run's timing.** The pin records today's resume, and the re-pin records the restart, after I have played it.
- **One source for the timing.** `run_frame_time` and `_run_clock` leave `rudy.gd`; the clip's keys become the only source of the run's timing. No existing test reads either of them.

### 2.2 Clip 2 — the slash (cutout rig, commits)

**Route:** cutout rig keyed as resource text. The agent writes the keys directly in `rudy_animations.tres`.

**Rig source.** `tools/cut_slash_rig.py` cuts parts from `game/content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-SLASH.png`, whose provenance is that of section 2.1. The parts go in `game/content/rudy/rig/`, each on the same 410 × 386 canvas with the same origin, so that at rest they register exactly on the original frame:
- `slash_body.png`: the frame without the blade and without the translucent arc. Where the arc crosses the robe and the shield, the script repairs the pixels from the surrounding robe and shield.
- `slash_blade.png`: the blade and crossguard, from the fist outwards.
- `slash_arc.png`: the translucent arc alone.

The script measures and prints the grip point (the centre of the fist around the hilt, near texture pixel (258, 165)). It checks that the three parts, composited at rest, equal the original frame except inside the repaired band, and it prints the size of that band. The parts are a derivative of my own generated art. The original frame stays as it is, and the script and the parts are committed as the rig's editable source.

**Rig nodes**, all under `Rudy/Look`, so they flip with `facing` and flash with the invulnerability fade as the Sprite does:

```text
Look
├── Sprite            Sprite2D, the sheet; hidden during the slash
├── SlashRig          Node2D, visible only during the slash
│   └── Lean          Node2D, pivot at his soles (0, 0); keyed position and rotation_degrees
│       ├── Grip      Node2D, pivot at the grip point; keyed rotation_degrees
│       │   └── Blade Sprite2D, slash_blade.png, drawn BEHIND Body
│       ├── Body      Sprite2D, slash_body.png
│       └── Arc       Sprite2D, slash_arc.png; keyed modulate:a; no outline material
└── AnimationPlayer
```

- **Draw order.** Blade comes before Body in the tree, so the fist covers the hilt and the blade's outline does not cross his hand.
- **Materials.** Body and Blade use the outline material; Arc does not, as the faint trail has none today (`outline.gdshader:8-9`).
- **Sprite settings.** Every part keeps the Sprite's offset and scale, so its canvas origin sits on Rudy's origin. Blade is offset from the Grip pivot so that, at Grip 0°, it sits where it was drawn.

**The phase table.** Frames are physics ticks at 60 per second, and tick 0 is the press tick. This is today's gameplay timing (section 1), which this change keeps. The clip's frame rate is 60, so a key's time is its tick divided by 60. The clip starts on tick 0, because the player is always playing a state clip when the slash starts (section 4).

| Phase | Ticks | Clip time | Hitbox (gameplay, unchanged) | What the rig does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Startup** | 0–1 | 0 – 2/60 s | dead | The blade is raised back over his shoulder (Grip −70° → −60°) and his weight sits back (Lean −2°). Two ticks: at 30 fps one rendered frame, so the wind-up reads as one held pose |
| **Active** | 2–10 | 2/60 – 11/60 s | **live** | The blade sweeps forward and down, accelerating: Grip −60° → 0° (the drawn angle) at tick 5 → +45° at tick 11. He leans into it (Lean +3°, x +6 px by tick 5). The arc appears at tick 2 (α 0 → 1 by tick 4) and fades by tick 11 |
| **Recovery** | 11–16 | 11/60 – 17/60 s | dead | The blade settles back: Grip +45° → +15°, decelerating. Lean returns to 0°, x 0 |
| **End** | 17 | 17/60 s | the swing ends (`rudy.gd:250-251`) | The clip's `length` is 17/60 s (0.2833 s). The state leaves `slash` on this tick, a cut to the sword form's idle, run or air pose |

**Keys at every phase boundary.** Key times are 0, 2/60, 5/60, 11/60 and 17/60 s, on these tracks:

| Track | 0 | 2/60 | 5/60 | 11/60 | 17/60 | Transitions |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `Look/Sprite:visible` (discrete) | false | | | | | |
| `Look/SlashRig:visible` (discrete) | true | | | | | |
| `Look/SlashRig/Lean/Grip:rotation_degrees` | −70 | −60 | 0 | 45 | 15 | ease-in (accelerating) into the active keys; ease-out (settling) from 11/60 |
| `Look/SlashRig/Lean:rotation_degrees` | −2 | −2 | 3 | 3 | 0 | ease-out from 11/60 |
| `Look/SlashRig/Lean:position` | (0, 0) | (0, 0) | (6, 0) | (6, 0) | (0, 0) | ease-out from 11/60 |
| `Look/SlashRig/Lean/Arc:modulate:a` | 0 | 0 | 1 (at 4/60) | 0 | 0 | linear |

- **Visibility.** Every other state clip keys `Sprite:visible` true and `SlashRig:visible` false at time 0, so leaving the slash on any tick shows the Sprite again.
- **Loop and positive angles.** `loop_mode` is `LOOP_NONE`. Positive angles turn clockwise on screen (y points down), so +45° points the blade forward and down.
- **The agent's key table.** The agent lists every key time beside the tick it comes from.

**Interrupts by phase.** These are unchanged gameplay rules, and the clip follows them:

| Event | Startup | Active | Recovery |
|---|---|---|---|
| Slash pressed again | ignored: no new swing, the clip is not restarted | ignored | ignored, including on tick 17 |
| Jump pressed on the floor | he jumps; the swing plays on in the air | the same | the same |
| Move or turn | he moves or turns; the rig flips with `Look` on the tick he turns | the same | the same |
| A hit (with the sword, it always knocks the sword away) | the swing ends on that tick: hurt clip, Sprite shown, rig hidden, hitbox dead | the same | the same |
| Fall out, respawn, teleport circle | the swing ends on that tick | the same | the same |
| Pause | the clip freezes with the tree; it goes on from the same point on resume | the same | the same |

## 3. The state machine

**Wiring: the existing priority list stays the single authority.** `rudy.gd` keeps choosing his state every physics tick with today's priorities, but the choice is now a clip name, not an asset ID. `RudyLook` plays that clip when it differs from the one playing. I chose this over an `AnimationTree`:
- **One authority.** The selector already is it. A tree with its own transitions would be a second machine that could disagree with it (Chapter 11).
- **No sampling gap.** The selector runs on every physics tick, so the gap Chapter 11 found between physics ticks and tree updates cannot open.
- **Nothing to blend.** There is nothing to cross-fade between whole frames.

Its weakness is the one Chapter 11 names for walker-jumpman-clawd: every change is a cut.

**The restart rule.** `play()` with the name already playing does not restart it (`evidence/brief-probe/logs/anim_clock_physics_60fps.log:13-14`). A new swing always follows at least one tick of another state (section 1), but `RudyLook` still starts every new swing with `play("slash")` and `seek(0.0, true)`, so the rule never rests on that gap.

**What keeps its meaning,** so that the existing checks pass unchanged:
- `Rudy.pose` is the asset ID of the pose on screen, read after the tick's animation update: the cell's pose while the Sprite shows, and `CHAR-SWORD-SLASH` while the rig shows.
- `RudyLook.FRAMES` maps every asset ID to its original PNG.
- `RudyLook.frame()` returns the original PNG of the pose on screen. During the slash that is `CHAR-SWORD-SLASH.png`, the frame the rig is cut from.

| 2 | `respawn` | cell 7 | `mode` is `RESPAWNING`, for `respawn_time` 0.7 s (`rudy.gd:177-190`) | one key, linear | cut |

- **Forms.** States 6 to 9 use the sword form's clip while `gear` is the sword.
- **Single-key clips loop.** They loop so that the player never stops: a `play()` on a stopped player shows its first key one tick late (`evidence/brief-probe/logs/anim_clock_physics_60fps.log:7-8`, against `:26-28`).
- **Cuts everywhere.** Whole frames cannot cross-fade, and the rig appears and disappears on a tick, so every transition is a cut on the tick its condition changes, as today.

## 4. Two clocks

- **Gameplay** runs in `rudy.gd`'s `_physics_process`, 60 ticks/s, and the hitbox stays there: `_swing()` reads `_slash_clock` (`rudy.gd:239-251`). **No animation key decides a gameplay fact.** The clip only draws; the hitbox, the slash sound (`rudy.gd:226`) and Effect A's sparks (which watch `SwordHitbox/Shape.disabled`, `game/effects/effects_driver.gd`) stay as they are.
- **The `AnimationPlayer`'s `callback_mode_process` is physics (0), set in the scene,** not the default idle (1) (`evidence/brief-probe/logs/anim_clock_physics_60fps.log:3`). In physics mode the clip time is (ticks since `play()`)/60 at 60 fps and at 30 fps alike (`anim_clock_physics_30fps.log:9-13`). In idle mode at 30 fps it advanced once per rendered frame, in uneven steps (0, 0.0292, 0.0592 s; `anim_clock_idle_30fps.log:7-13`): a second clock that would let the rig's active keys drift off the live ticks.
- **Order within a tick.** The player is a child of `Look`, which is a child of `Rudy`, and in the probe a child's physics processing ran after its host's `_physics_process` on the same tick. So a `play()` from `rudy.gd` on tick 0 shows the clip's first key on tick 0, provided the player was already playing (`anim_clock_physics_60fps.log:27-28`).
- **Method callbacks** stay deferred (the default, 0). No clip has a method track, so nothing depends on when a method key runs.
- **No `AnimatedSprite2D`** is used, so no second sprite clock exists.
- **The rendered frame.** Tests run at `--fixed-fps 60`: one tick per frame. Movie Maker captures run at 30 fps: two ticks per frame, and each PNG shows the state after the frame's second tick.

| Rule | Checked by | How |
|---|---|---|
| Every clip's tracks, keys, loop and update modes; the player's settings; the sheet's slicing | headless: read-back test | `test_rudy_clips.tscn`, section 9 |

## 12. How the agent sessions run

The rules below are the ones the assignment states; the source of each is in brackets.

- **One step per prompt.** One bounded step per prompt and one commit per verified step [course text, "Pin first, then change"]. Each prompt runs as its own Claude Code session with stream-JSON output, as in Chapter 10's command.
- **Git is read-only for the agent** (status, diff, log, show) [revision note, "Keep read-only git"].
- **The result event.** A session counts only if its stream-JSON ends with a `result` event whose subtype is `success` [revision note, "the result-event check"]. A session that ends any other way, at a usage limit or a turn limit, is **interrupted**.
- **Resuming** [revision note, "Add a rule for resuming interrupted sessions"]. An interrupted session's uncommitted work is not built on. I inspect its diff and rerun its checks through the wrapper. Then either I commit it as its own verified step, or I discard it with `git restore` and `git clean` limited to the files it touched. Only then does a new session start, with a prompt that says what the old one left.
- **Mutation checks** run in a `git worktree` of the pre-fix commit [revision note, "use git worktree for the mutation check"].
- **Committing.** Commits are mine, in the order worked: baseline, pin, each change, each fix, each re-pin [course text, "Commit in the order you worked"].

- No `AnimationTree`, no `AnimatedSprite2D`, no method or audio tracks: the slash sound stays in code.
- No gameplay change, including the slash's 2-tick startup.
- The goblins keep their code-picked frames (`goblin.gd:112-118`). `CHAR-SWORD-BLOCK` stays unused, as today (`checks.gd:879-882`).

## Godot 4 names (probed on 4.7.2: `evidence/brief-probe/README.md`)

- Write `loop_mode`, not `loop`. 4.7.2 happens to map `loop = true`, but Godot 4 code uses `loop_mode`.
- Write `speed_scale`, not `playback_speed`: `playback_speed` is dropped without a message.

- A track to a missing property prints nothing. If you are unsure a property exists in 4.7.2, check it (`ClassDB`, or load and read back) instead of guessing.

## Git

Git is read-only for the agent: `status`, `diff`, `log`, `show`. Do not commit, stage, stash, reset, switch branches or delete files with git; commits are mine.

#   - Godot is $GODOT if set, else godot on PATH, else the macOS app's binary.
#   - It runs from this folder wherever it is called from, so the project path
#     resolves and the logs land in its logs/.

# loads a scene whose texture or sub-scene is missing, instances it and exits
# 0, saying so only in the log (evidence/load-error-probe/). So besides SHADER
# ERROR and SCRIPT ERROR, the run fails on these lines from that probe:
#   Cannot open file          a file that does not exist
#   Failed loading resource   any load that returned null
#   Resource file not found   a missing ext_resource or typed load
#   Parse Error               a broken .tres/.tscn, or an ext_resource that
#                             names a missing file (the scene still loads)
#   Error loading resource    ResourceLoader.load() of a missing file
#   Failed to load script     a script that does not compile
#   couldn't resolve track    an animation track naming a node that does not
#                             exist (a WARNING; a missing property prints
#                             nothing, so the read-back test must check that)
# When one of these fails the run, the wrapper prints the lines it matched.
# Unchanged from the course: the realtime mode (no --fixed-fps, for tests that
# wait on audio), the optional timeout (120 s by default; status 124 means the
# test hung), the log name logs/<test>_<fps>fps.log or logs/<test>_realtime.log,
# and that exit code 0 does not mean no errors.
set -o pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." || exit 2
if [ $# -lt 2 ] || [ $# -gt 3 ] || [ ! -f "game/tests/$1" ]; then
	echo "usage: scripts/run-test.sh <test-file in game/tests/> <fps|realtime> [timeout-seconds]" >&2
	exit 2
fi
godot=${GODOT:-$(command -v godot || echo /Applications/Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot)}
if [ "$2" = "realtime" ]; then
	fps_args=(); tag="realtime"
else
	fps_args=(--fixed-fps "$2"); tag="${2}fps"
fi
if [[ $1 == *.tscn ]]; then
	run_args=("res://tests/$1")
else
	run_args=(--script "res://tests/$1")
fi
mkdir -p logs
log="logs/$(basename "${1%.*}")_${tag}.log"
timeout "${3:-120}" "$godot" --headless "${fps_args[@]}" --path game "${run_args[@]}" 2>&1 | tee "$log"
status=$?
errors="SHADER ERROR|SCRIPT ERROR|Cannot open file|Failed loading resource|Resource file not found|Parse Error|Error loading resource|Failed to load script|couldn't resolve track"
if grep -qE "$errors" "$log"; then
	echo "run-test.sh: FAILED on an error line in $log:" >&2
	grep -nE "$errors" "$log" >&2

1	class_name Rudy
2	extends CharacterBody2D
3	## Rudy's controller. It moves him and picks the clip that shows his state
4	## (_pick_clip); his Look plays that clip on its AnimationPlayer, which draws
5	## the pose's frame from the sheet. `pose` is the asset ID in
6	## CHARACTER-SHEET.md of the pose on screen. The origin is at his soles.
7	##
8	## In the air he shows the rising pose, and the falling pose only if he was
9	## moving sideways when the fall began. The falling pose leaps forward, so a
10	## jump straight up keeps the rising pose all the way down; the pose changes
11	## at most once in the air, at the top.
12	##
13	## On the ground, pressing the other direction turns him in place at once, with
14	## no slide; he moves that way only if the key is still held after
15	## turn_hold_time, so a tap turns him without moving him or the camera.
16	##
17	## Gear: the sword-and-shield pickup gives him the sword form, with its own
18	## poses (CHAR-SWORD-*). A fresh press of slash swings the sword once; its
19	## hitbox in front of him is live for part of the swing, and one cut defeats a
20	## goblin. No new swing starts until the last one ends.
21	##
22	## Damage (CHANGE-BRIEF.md): a hit knocks his gear away if he carries it, and
23	## otherwise costs one of his hearts. Either way it turns him toward the hit,
24	## knocks him back and makes him invulnerable for a moment, flashing; hits
25	## during that window are ignored. A fall below a cliff costs a heart too. At
26	## zero hearts he is defeated, and the level starts over from the opening, with
27	## his hearts full. He can only be hit by the collision capsule, so a hit that
28	## grazes his hair, his sword or his shield is a miss.
29	##
30	## The level also takes control away when he falls out of the level, while he
31	## gets back up after a respawn (always without gear), and while he celebrates
32	## on the teleport circle.
33	##
34	## The feel numbers are tuned by playtesting.
35	
36	signal respawned ## he has got back up after a respawn, and control returns
37	signal hit ## a hit has just cost him his gear or a heart
38	signal hearts_changed(hearts: int)
39	signal defeated ## a hit took his last heart
40	
41	enum Mode {
42		WAITING, ## on the title, before play starts (CHAR-IDLE); no control
43		PLAY, ## under the player's control
44		HURT, ## knocked back by a hit (CHAR-HURT); no control for hurt_time
45		DEFEATED, ## his last heart is gone (CHAR-DEFEAT); no control
46		FALLEN, ## fell below a cliff; no control
47		RESPAWNING, ## getting back up at a checkpoint (CHAR-RESPAWN); no control
48		CELEBRATING, ## on the teleport circle (CHAR-CELEBRATE); no control
49	}
50	
51	enum Gear { NONE, SWORD }
52	
53	const ENEMY_LAYER := 4 ## the Enemy physics layer, for the sword's hitbox
54	
55	@export_group("Feel")
56	@export var run_speed := 560.0 ## px/s
57	@export var run_accel := 5600.0 ## px/s²: full speed, or a stop, in 0.1 s
58	@export var turn_hold_time := 0.12 ## s the key is held after a turn on the ground before he moves
59	@export var gravity := 4000.0 ## px/s² on the way up
60	@export var fall_gravity := 6400.0 ## px/s² on the way down, so the fall is quicker than the rise
61	@export var jump_velocity := 1500.0 ## px/s; at 60 physics ticks/s the apex is 294 px, the rise takes 0.38 s and the fall 0.32 s
62	@export var respawn_time := 0.7 ## s in CHAR-RESPAWN before control returns
63	@export var stomp_bounce := 600.0 ## px/s upward after he lands on an enemy
64	
65	@export_group("Sword")
66	@export var slash_time := 0.3 ## s a swing lasts (CHAR-SWORD-SLASH); no new swing until it ends
67	@export var slash_live_from := 0.03 ## s into the swing when the hitbox goes live
68	@export var slash_live_to := 0.18 ## s into the swing when it goes dead again
69	@export var slash_reach := 50.0 ## px from his centre to the centre of the hitbox, in front of him
70	
71	@export_group("Damage")
72	@export var max_hearts := 3
73	@export var knockback := Vector2(350, 400) ## px/s: away from the hit, and up
74	@export var hurt_time := 0.35 ## s without control after a hit
75	@export var invulnerable_time := 1.2 ## s after a hit or a respawn in which hits are ignored
76	@export var flash_period := 0.12 ## s; he is see-through for half of each period while invulnerable
77	
78	var facing := 1 ## 1 faces right, -1 faces left
79	## The asset ID of the pose on screen, read from the cell his Look's Sprite shows.
80	var pose: StringName:
81		get:
82			return _look.pose if _look else &"CHAR-IDLE"
83	var mode := Mode.PLAY ## the level sets WAITING while the title shows
84	var hearts := 3
85	var gear := Gear.NONE
86	
87	var _turn_time_left := 0.0
88	var _respawn_time_left := 0.0
89	var _hurt_time_left := 0.0
90	var _invulnerable_left := 0.0
91	var _bounce_pending := false
92	var _was_falling := false
93	var _falls_sideways := false ## whether he was moving sideways when this fall began
94	var _slash_clock := -1.0 ## s into the current swing; below 0 when he is not swinging
95	var _slash_query := PhysicsShapeQueryParameters2D.new()
96	
97	@onready var _look: RudyLook = $Look
98	@onready var _sword_box: CollisionShape2D = $SwordHitbox/Shape
99	
100	
101	func _ready() -> void:
102		hearts = max_hearts
103		_slash_query.shape = _sword_box.shape
104		_slash_query.collision_mask = ENEMY_LAYER
105		_slash_query.collide_with_areas = true
106		_slash_query.collide_with_bodies = false
107		# The player is never stopped when a state starts: it plays idle (cell 0,
108		# the Sprite's frame before the first tick) from the start.
109		_look.play_clip(&"idle")
110	
111	
112	## True while enemies and hazards can touch him: in play, or knocked back.
113	func can_be_touched() -> bool:
114		return mode == Mode.PLAY or mode == Mode.HURT
115	
116	
117	func is_invulnerable() -> bool:
118		return _invulnerable_left > 0.0
119	
120	
121	func is_slashing() -> bool:
122		return _slash_clock >= 0.0
123	
124	
125	## The pickup gives him the sword and shield.
126	func equip_sword() -> void:
127		gear = Gear.SWORD
128	
129	
130	## A hit from something at `from`. It knocks his gear away if he has any, and
131	## otherwise costs a heart, unless he cannot be touched or is still
132	## invulnerable; returns whether it did.
133	func take_hit(from: Vector2) -> bool:
134		if not can_be_touched() or is_invulnerable():
135			return false
136		var away := signf(global_position.x - from.x)
137		if away == 0.0:
138			away = -facing
139		var lost_gear := gear != Gear.NONE
140		if lost_gear:
141			_drop_gear(away)
142		else:
143			hearts -= 1
144			hearts_changed.emit(hearts)
145		Sfx.play(&"hurt")
146		facing = -int(away) # he turns toward the hit
147		_turn_time_left = 0.0
148		_slash_clock = -1.0
149		_invulnerable_left = invulnerable_time
150		hit.emit()
151		if not lost_gear and hearts <= 0:
152			mode = Mode.DEFEATED
153			velocity.x = 0.0
154			defeated.emit()
155		else:
156			mode = Mode.HURT
157			_hurt_time_left = hurt_time
158			velocity = Vector2(away * knockback.x, -knockback.y)
159		return true
160	
161	
162	## He landed on an enemy from above. The bounce starts on his next tick, so
163	## every enemy he lands on in the same tick sees him still falling.
164	func bounce() -> void:
165		_bounce_pending = true
166	
167	
168	## He fell below a cliff: he keeps falling, out of the player's control, and
169	## the fall costs a heart (with no knockback; the level plays the hurt sound as
170	## he crosses the kill line). Returns whether it was his last heart.
171	func fall_out() -> bool:
172		mode = Mode.FALLEN
173		_slash_clock = -1.0
174		hearts = maxi(hearts - 1, 0)
175		hearts_changed.emit(hearts)
176		return hearts == 0
177	
178	
179	## Puts him back on his feet at a checkpoint, without gear, facing right,
180	## getting back up, and invulnerable for a moment. After a defeat his hearts are
181	## full again; after a fall he keeps the ones he has left.
182	func respawn_at(spot: Vector2, refill_hearts: bool) -> void:
183		global_position = spot
184		velocity = Vector2.ZERO
185		facing = 1
186		gear = Gear.NONE
187		_slash_clock = -1.0
188		_turn_time_left = 0.0
189		_bounce_pending = false
190		if refill_hearts:
191			hearts = max_hearts
192			hearts_changed.emit(hearts)
193		_invulnerable_left = invulnerable_time
194		mode = Mode.RESPAWNING
195		_respawn_time_left = respawn_time
196	
197	
198	func celebrate() -> void:
199		mode = Mode.CELEBRATING
200		_slash_clock = -1.0
201	
202	
203	func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
204		if _bounce_pending:
205			_bounce_pending = false
206			velocity.y = -stomp_bounce
207		var in_control := mode == Mode.PLAY
208		var dir := _input_direction() if in_control else 0
209		if dir != 0 and dir != facing:
210			facing = dir
211			if is_on_floor():
212				velocity.x = 0.0
213				_turn_time_left = turn_hold_time
214		if dir == 0 or not is_on_floor():
215			_turn_time_left = 0.0
216		_turn_time_left = maxf(_turn_time_left - delta, 0.0)
217		if not (mode == Mode.HURT and not is_on_floor()):
218			# A knockback carries him until he lands; otherwise run, or slow down.
219			var target_speed := 0.0 if _turn_time_left > 0.0 else dir * run_speed
220			velocity.x = move_toward(velocity.x, target_speed, run_accel * delta)
221	
222		if not is_on_floor():
223			velocity.y += (fall_gravity if velocity.y >= 0.0 else gravity) * delta
224		elif in_control and Input.is_action_just_pressed(&"jump"):
225			# A fresh press with ground underfoot: holding the key cannot jump again.
226			velocity.y = -jump_velocity
227			Sfx.play(&"jump")
228		var new_swing := false
229		if in_control and gear == Gear.SWORD and not is_slashing() and Input.is_action_just_pressed(&"slash"):
230			# A fresh press, and not while a swing is under way: one sound per swing.
231			_slash_clock = 0.0
232			new_swing = true
233			Sfx.play(&"slash")
234		move_and_slide()
235	
236		_swing(delta)
237		_count_down(delta)
238		_look.scale.x = facing
239		_look.modulate.a = 0.35 if is_invulnerable() and fmod(_invulnerable_left, flash_period) < flash_period / 2.0 else 1.0
240		# Every new swing starts the slash clip over from its first key.
241		_look.play_clip(_pick_clip(), new_swing)
242	
243	
244	## Moves the swing on and, while its hitbox is live, defeats every goblin in it.
245	## It asks the physics space directly, so the cut lands on the tick it reaches.
246	func _swing(delta: float) -> void:
247		_sword_box.position.x = slash_reach * facing
248		var live := is_slashing() and _slash_clock >= slash_live_from and _slash_clock <= slash_live_to
249		_sword_box.disabled = not live
250		if live:
251			_slash_query.transform = _sword_box.global_transform
252			for contact in get_world_2d().direct_space_state.intersect_shape(_slash_query, 8):
253				if contact.collider is Goblin:
254					(contact.collider as Goblin).defeat(&"slash")
255		if is_slashing():
256			_slash_clock += delta
257			if _slash_clock >= slash_time:
258				_slash_clock = -1.0
259	
260	
261	## The gear flies off, up and away from the hit, and fades.
262	func _drop_gear(away: float) -> void:
263		gear = Gear.NONE
264		var flying := FlyingGear.new()
265		flying.position = global_position + Vector2(0, -80)
266		flying.velocity = Vector2(away * 220.0, -420.0)
267		get_parent().add_child(flying)
268	
269	
270	func _count_down(delta: float) -> void:
271		_invulnerable_left = maxf(_invulnerable_left - delta, 0.0)
272		if mode == Mode.HURT:
273			_hurt_time_left -= delta
274			if _hurt_time_left <= 0.0:
275				mode = Mode.PLAY
276		elif mode == Mode.RESPAWNING:
277			_respawn_time_left -= delta
278			if _respawn_time_left <= 0.0:
279				mode = Mode.PLAY
280				respawned.emit()
281	
282	
283	func _input_direction() -> int:
284		var axis := Input.get_axis(&"move_left", &"move_right")
285		if axis > 0.0:
286			return 1
287		if axis < 0.0:
288			return -1
289		return 0
290	
291	
292	## The clip for his state, by today's priorities (CHANGE-BRIEF.md section 3):
293	## higher in the list wins. Every name it returns is a StringName literal, so
294	## the read-back test can read them all from this file's text. The run's
295	## timing lives in the run clips' keys.
296	func _pick_clip() -> StringName:
297		match mode:
298			Mode.CELEBRATING:
299				return &"celebrate"
300			Mode.RESPAWNING:
301				return &"respawn"
302			Mode.DEFEATED:
303				return &"defeat"
304			Mode.HURT:
305				return &"hurt"
306		if is_slashing():
307			return &"slash"
308		var sword := gear == Gear.SWORD
309		if not is_on_floor():
310			var falling := velocity.y >= 0.0
311			if falling and not _was_falling:
312				_falls_sideways = absf(velocity.x) > 1.0
313			_was_falling = falling
314			if falling and _falls_sideways:
315				return &"sword_fall" if sword else &"fall"
316			return &"sword_rise" if sword else &"rise"
317		_was_falling = false
318		if absf(velocity.x) > 1.0:
319			return &"sword_run" if sword else &"run"
320		return &"sword_idle" if sword else &"idle"
321

## moving sideways when the fall began. The falling pose leaps forward, so a
## jump straight up keeps the rising pose all the way down; the pose changes
## at most once in the air, at the top.
##
## On the ground, pressing the other direction turns him in place at once, with
## no slide; he moves that way only if the key is still held after
## turn_hold_time, so a tap turns him without moving him or the camera.
##
## Gear: the sword-and-shield pickup gives him the sword form, with its own
## poses (CHAR-SWORD-*). A fresh press of slash swings the sword once; its
## hitbox in front of him is live for part of the swing, and one cut defeats a
## goblin. No new swing starts until the last one ends.
##
## Damage (CHANGE-BRIEF.md): a hit knocks his gear away if he carries it, and
## otherwise costs one of his hearts. Either way it turns him toward the hit,
## knocks him back and makes him invulnerable for a moment, flashing; hits
## during that window are ignored. A fall below a cliff costs a heart too. At
## zero hearts he is defeated, and the level starts over from the opening, with
## his hearts full. He can only be hit by the collision capsule, so a hit that
## grazes his hair, his sword or his shield is a miss.
##
## The level also takes control away when he falls out of the level, while he
## gets back up after a respawn (always without gear), and while he celebrates
## on the teleport circle.
##
## The feel numbers are tuned by playtesting.

signal respawned ## he has got back up after a respawn, and control returns
signal hit ## a hit has just cost him his gear or a heart
signal hearts_changed(hearts: int)
signal defeated ## a hit took his last heart

enum Mode {
	WAITING, ## on the title, before play starts (CHAR-IDLE); no control
	PLAY, ## under the player's control
	HURT, ## knocked back by a hit (CHAR-HURT); no control for hurt_time
	DEFEATED, ## his last heart is gone (CHAR-DEFEAT); no control
	FALLEN, ## fell below a cliff; no control
	RESPAWNING, ## getting back up at a checkpoint (CHAR-RESPAWN); no control
	CELEBRATING, ## on the teleport circle (CHAR-CELEBRATE); no control
}

enum Gear { NONE, SWORD }

const ENEMY_LAYER := 4 ## the Enemy physics layer, for the sword's hitbox

@export_group("Feel")
@export var run_speed := 560.0 ## px/s
@export var run_accel := 5600.0 ## px/s²: full speed, or a stop, in 0.1 s
@export var turn_hold_time := 0.12 ## s the key is held after a turn on the ground before he moves
@export var gravity := 4000.0 ## px/s² on the way up
@export var fall_gravity := 6400.0 ## px/s² on the way down, so the fall is quicker than the rise
@export var jump_velocity := 1500.0 ## px/s; at 60 physics ticks/s the apex is 294 px, the rise takes 0.38 s and the fall 0.32 s
@export var respawn_time := 0.7 ## s in CHAR-RESPAWN before control returns
@export var stomp_bounce := 600.0 ## px/s upward after he lands on an enemy

@export_group("Sword")
@export var slash_time := 0.3 ## s a swing lasts (CHAR-SWORD-SLASH); no new swing until it ends
@export var slash_live_from := 0.03 ## s into the swing when the hitbox goes live
@export var slash_live_to := 0.18 ## s into the swing when it goes dead again
@export var slash_reach := 50.0 ## px from his centre to the centre of the hitbox, in front of him

@export_group("Damage")
@export var max_hearts := 3
@export var knockback := Vector2(350, 400) ## px/s: away from the hit, and up
@export var hurt_time := 0.35 ## s without control after a hit
@export var invulnerable_time := 1.2 ## s after a hit or a respawn in which hits are ignored
@export var flash_period := 0.12 ## s; he is see-through for half of each period while invulnerable

var facing := 1 ## 1 faces right, -1 faces left
## The asset ID of the pose on screen, read from the cell his Look's Sprite shows.
var pose: StringName:
	get:
		return _look.pose if _look else &"CHAR-IDLE"
var mode := Mode.PLAY ## the level sets WAITING while the title shows
var hearts := 3
var gear := Gear.NONE

var _turn_time_left := 0.0
var _respawn_time_left := 0.0
var _hurt_time_left := 0.0
var _invulnerable_left := 0.0
var _bounce_pending := false
var _was_falling := false
var _falls_sideways := false ## whether he was moving sideways when this fall began
var _slash_clock := -1.0 ## s into the current swing; below 0 when he is not swinging
var _slash_query := PhysicsShapeQueryParameters2D.new()

@onready var _look: RudyLook = $Look
@onready var _sword_box: CollisionShape2D = $SwordHitbox/Shape


func _ready() -> void:
	hearts = max_hearts
	_slash_query.shape = _sword_box.shape
	_slash_query.collision_mask = ENEMY_LAYER
	_slash_query.collide_with_areas = true
	_slash_query.collide_with_bodies = false

	# the Sprite's frame before the first tick) from the start.
	_look.play_clip(&"idle")


## True while enemies and hazards can touch him: in play, or knocked back.
func can_be_touched() -> bool:
	return mode == Mode.PLAY or mode == Mode.HURT


func is_invulnerable() -> bool:
	return _invulnerable_left > 0.0


func is_slashing() -> bool:
	return _slash_clock >= 0.0


## The pickup gives him the sword and shield.
func equip_sword() -> void:
	gear = Gear.SWORD


## A hit from something at `from`. It knocks his gear away if he has any, and
## otherwise costs a heart, unless he cannot be touched or is still
## invulnerable; returns whether it did.
func take_hit(from: Vector2) -> bool:
	if not can_be_touched() or is_invulnerable():
		return false
	var away := signf(global_position.x - from.x)
	if away == 0.0:
		away = -facing
	var lost_gear := gear != Gear.NONE
	if lost_gear:
		_drop_gear(away)
	else:
		hearts -= 1
		hearts_changed.emit(hearts)
	Sfx.play(&"hurt")
	facing = -int(away) # he turns toward the hit
	_turn_time_left = 0.0
	_slash_clock = -1.0
	_invulnerable_left = invulnerable_time
	hit.emit()
	if not lost_gear and hearts <= 0:
		mode = Mode.DEFEATED
		velocity.x = 0.0
		defeated.emit()
	else:
		mode = Mode.HURT
		_hurt_time_left = hurt_time
		velocity = Vector2(away * knockback.x, -knockback.y)
	return true


## He landed on an enemy from above. The bounce starts on his next tick, so
## every enemy he lands on in the same tick sees him still falling.
func bounce() -> void:
	_bounce_pending = true


## He fell below a cliff: he keeps falling, out of the player's control, and
## the fall costs a heart (with no knockback; the level plays the hurt sound as
## he crosses the kill line). Returns whether it was his last heart.
func fall_out() -> bool:
	mode = Mode.FALLEN
	_slash_clock = -1.0
	hearts = maxi(hearts - 1, 0)
	hearts_changed.emit(hearts)
	return hearts == 0


## Puts him back on his feet at a checkpoint, without gear, facing right,
## getting back up, and invulnerable for a moment. After a defeat his hearts are
## full again; after a fall he keeps the ones he has left.
func respawn_at(spot: Vector2, refill_hearts: bool) -> void:
	global_position = spot
	velocity = Vector2.ZERO
	facing = 1
	gear = Gear.NONE
	_slash_clock = -1.0
	_turn_time_left = 0.0
	_bounce_pending = false
	if refill_hearts:
		hearts = max_hearts
		hearts_changed.emit(hearts)
	_invulnerable_left = invulnerable_time
	mode = Mode.RESPAWNING
	_respawn_time_left = respawn_time


func celebrate() -> void:
	mode = Mode.CELEBRATING
	_slash_clock = -1.0


func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	if _bounce_pending:
		_bounce_pending = false
		velocity.y = -stomp_bounce
	var in_control := mode == Mode.PLAY
	var dir := _input_direction() if in_control else 0
	if dir != 0 and dir != facing:
		facing = dir
		if is_on_floor():
			velocity.x = 0.0
			_turn_time_left = turn_hold_time
	if dir == 0 or not is_on_floor():
		_turn_time_left = 0.0
	_turn_time_left = maxf(_turn_time_left - delta, 0.0)
	if not (mode == Mode.HURT and not is_on_floor()):
		# A knockback carries him until he lands; otherwise run, or slow down.
		var target_speed := 0.0 if _turn_time_left > 0.0 else dir * run_speed
		velocity.x = move_toward(velocity.x, target_speed, run_accel * delta)

	if not is_on_floor():
		velocity.y += (fall_gravity if velocity.y >= 0.0 else gravity) * delta
	elif in_control and Input.is_action_just_pressed(&"jump"):
		# A fresh press with ground underfoot: holding the key cannot jump again.
		velocity.y = -jump_velocity
		Sfx.play(&"jump")
	var new_swing := false
	if in_control and gear == Gear.SWORD and not is_slashing() and Input.is_action_just_pressed(&"slash"):
		# A fresh press, and not while a swing is under way: one sound per swing.
		_slash_clock = 0.0
		new_swing = true
		Sfx.play(&"slash")
	move_and_slide()

	_swing(delta)
	_count_down(delta)
	_look.scale.x = facing
	_look.modulate.a = 0.35 if is_invulnerable() and fmod(_invulnerable_left, flash_period) < flash_period / 2.0 else 1.0
	# Every new swing starts the slash clip over from its first key.
	_look.play_clip(_pick_clip(), new_swing)


## Moves the swing on and, while its hitbox is live, defeats every goblin in it.
## It asks the physics space directly, so the cut lands on the tick it reaches.
func _swing(delta: float) -> void:
	_sword_box.position.x = slash_reach * facing
	var live := is_slashing() and _slash_clock >= slash_live_from and _slash_clock <= slash_live_to
	_sword_box.disabled = not live
	if live:
		_slash_query.transform = _sword_box.global_transform
		for contact in get_world_2d().direct_space_state.intersect_shape(_slash_query, 8):
			if contact.collider is Goblin:
				(contact.collider as Goblin).defeat(&"slash")
	if is_slashing():
		_slash_clock += delta
		if _slash_clock >= slash_time:
			_slash_clock = -1.0


## The gear flies off, up and away from the hit, and fades.
func _drop_gear(away: float) -> void:
	gear = Gear.NONE
	var flying := FlyingGear.new()
	flying.position = global_position + Vector2(0, -80)
	flying.velocity = Vector2(away * 220.0, -420.0)
	get_parent().add_child(flying)


func _count_down(delta: float) -> void:
	_invulnerable_left = maxf(_invulnerable_left - delta, 0.0)
	if mode == Mode.HURT:
		_hurt_time_left -= delta
		if _hurt_time_left <= 0.0:
			mode = Mode.PLAY
	elif mode == Mode.RESPAWNING:
		_respawn_time_left -= delta
		if _respawn_time_left <= 0.0:
			mode = Mode.PLAY
			respawned.emit()


func _input_direction() -> int:
	var axis := Input.get_axis(&"move_left", &"move_right")
	if axis > 0.0:
		return 1
	if axis < 0.0:
		return -1
	return 0


## The clip for his state, by today's priorities (CHANGE-BRIEF.md section 3):
## higher in the list wins. Every name it returns is a StringName literal, so
## the read-back test can read them all from this file's text. The run's
## timing lives in the run clips' keys.
func _pick_clip() -> StringName:
	match mode:
		Mode.CELEBRATING:
			return &"celebrate"
		Mode.RESPAWNING:
			return &"respawn"
		Mode.DEFEATED:
			return &"defeat"
		Mode.HURT:
			return &"hurt"
	if is_slashing():
		return &"slash"
	var sword := gear == Gear.SWORD
	if not is_on_floor():
		var falling := velocity.y >= 0.0
		if falling and not _was_falling:
			_falls_sideways = absf(velocity.x) > 1.0
		_was_falling = falling
		if falling and _falls_sideways:
			return &"sword_fall" if sword else &"fall"
		return &"sword_rise" if sword else &"rise"
	_was_falling = false
	if absf(velocity.x) > 1.0:
		return &"sword_run" if sword else &"run"
	return &"sword_idle" if sword else &"idle"
