class_name RudyLook
extends Node2D
## Rudy's generated frames (ASSET-LOG.md), one per pose asset ID in
## CHARACTER-SHEET.md, made by design/tools/matte_sprites.py into frames/.
## Every frame shares one canvas with the body origin (his soles, on the
## torso's centre line) at the same texture px, and is stored at 2 texture px
## per game px; the Sprite child draws it at half scale with that origin on
## this node's, as frames.json says. The controller flips this node to face
## left and fades it while he flashes. The Sprite's material adds the outer
## outline (systems/art/outline.gdshader), and it draws with mipmaps so the
## hair's fine lines do not shimmer at half scale.
## The sword form's frames show the sword and shield he holds, so nothing is
## drawn over them. CHAR-SWORD-BLOCK waits for blocking (build step 4).
##
## The Sprite draws the 16 frames from one sheet, sheet/rudy_sheet.png (4 x 4
## cells, in frames.json's order: CELLS). Its AnimationPlayer is the only
## writer of the Sprite's frame: this script plays the clip the controller
## picks and never sets the Sprite's texture or frame (CHANGE-BRIEF.md
## section 5). The pose on screen is read back from what is drawn: while the
## slash's cutout rig (SlashRig) shows, it is CHAR-SWORD-SLASH, the frame the
## rig is cut from; otherwise it is the pose of the cell the Sprite shows. The
## player is also the only writer of SlashRig's and the Sprite's visibility:
## this script only reads them (section 3).

const FRAMES: Dictionary[StringName, Texture2D] = {
	&"CHAR-IDLE": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-IDLE.png"),
	&"CHAR-RUN-A": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-RUN-A.png"),
	&"CHAR-RUN-B": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-RUN-B.png"),
	&"CHAR-RISE": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-RISE.png"),
	&"CHAR-FALL": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-FALL.png"),
	&"CHAR-HURT": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-HURT.png"),
	&"CHAR-DEFEAT": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-DEFEAT.png"),
	&"CHAR-RESPAWN": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-RESPAWN.png"),
	&"CHAR-CELEBRATE": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-CELEBRATE.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-IDLE": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-IDLE.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-RUN-A": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-RUN-A.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-RUN-B": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-RUN-B.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-RISE": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-RISE.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-FALL": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-FALL.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-SLASH": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-SLASH.png"),
	&"CHAR-SWORD-BLOCK": preload("res://content/rudy/frames/CHAR-SWORD-BLOCK.png"),
}

## The sheet's cells, row by row: cell N shows the frame of CELLS[N]. This is
## frames.json's order (CHANGE-BRIEF.md section 2.1).
const CELLS: Array[StringName] = [
	&"CHAR-IDLE", &"CHAR-RUN-A", &"CHAR-RUN-B", &"CHAR-RISE",
	&"CHAR-FALL", &"CHAR-HURT", &"CHAR-DEFEAT", &"CHAR-RESPAWN",
	&"CHAR-CELEBRATE", &"CHAR-SWORD-IDLE", &"CHAR-SWORD-SLASH", &"CHAR-SWORD-BLOCK",
	&"CHAR-SWORD-RUN-A", &"CHAR-SWORD-RUN-B", &"CHAR-SWORD-RISE", &"CHAR-SWORD-FALL",
]

## The pose the slash rig draws: the frame its parts are cut from (section 2.2).
const RIG_POSE := &"CHAR-SWORD-SLASH"

## The asset ID of the pose on screen: RIG_POSE while SlashRig shows, else the
## pose of the cell the Sprite shows. It reads the nodes, not the clip asked
## for, and finds them by path, so it also reads true on a copy of Rudy that
## is not in the tree.
var pose: StringName:
	get:
		var rig := get_node_or_null(^"SlashRig") as CanvasItem
		if rig != null and rig.visible:
			return RIG_POSE
		var sprite := get_node_or_null(^"Sprite") as Sprite2D
		return CELLS[sprite.frame] if sprite else CELLS[0]

@onready var _player: AnimationPlayer = $AnimationPlayer


## Plays `clip` if it is not the clip playing. `restart` starts it over from
## its first key even if it is playing: every new swing does (section 3).
## The seek comes before play(): play() marks the clip as just started, so
## the player's update later this tick adds no time and shows the first key
## on this tick. A seek(0.0, true) after play() would run that update at once,
## using the mark up, and the tick's own update would then add a tick: the
## slash would end, and the player stop, a tick early.
func play_clip(clip: StringName, restart := false) -> void:
	if not restart and StringName(_player.current_animation) == clip:
		return
	if restart:
		_player.seek(0.0, true)
	_player.play(clip)


## The frame on screen now: the original PNG of the pose on screen. While the
## rig shows, that is CHAR-SWORD-SLASH.png, the frame the rig is cut from.
func frame() -> Texture2D:
	return FRAMES[pose]

1	extends Node
2	## The edge test (CHANGE-BRIEF.md sections 6 and 9; step 5b). Run from the
3	## assignment folder:
4	##   scripts/run-test.sh test_rudy_edges.tscn 60
5	##   scripts/run-test.sh test_rudy_edges.tscn 30
6	##
7	## It works out how many physics ticks a rendered frame holds. With one (60
8	## fps) it runs E1-E7; with two (30 fps) it runs E1 and E2, once at each tick
9	## offset. Every edge is checked tick by tick, in physics ticks from the press.
10	##
11	## Rules this test keeps (the state test's, test_rudy_states.gd):
12	## - Each scenario starts a fresh real Main with the title skipped, as
13	##   checks.gd's _start_level() does (Main.title_shown = true before it is
14	##   instanced). E3's goblins and E6's pause need it.
15	## - Setup comes before a scenario's first key, and only then: it may place
16	##   Rudy at a spot on the level and lets him settle. From the first key on,
17	##   nothing writes his state, velocity, position, gear, hearts or mode. He
18	##   takes the sword by walking into the pickup.
19	## - Input is only InputEventKey events for the project's physical keys D, A,
20	##   Space, J and Esc, sent with Input.parse_input_event. A fresh press of a
21	##   key that is still held sends its key-up and key-down together, as the pin
22	##   does (test_rudy_pin.gd, step 5b).
23	## - It reads properties (Rudy's _slash_clock among them, read only), and
24	##   calls only read-only queries: is_on_floor(), get_children(), the
25	##   AnimationPlayer's current_animation and current_animation_position, and
26	##   Input's is_action_just_pressed()/is_action_just_released(). It never calls
27	##   play(), seek(), advance() or a state method.
28	## - This node is the recorder. Its process_physics_priority is 100, so on
29	##   every tick it samples after Rudy, his AnimationPlayer and the effects
30	##   driver: sample N is what tick N left.
31	##
32	## Pausing. Esc pauses the tree (Main.toggle_pause, from SystemKeys). So that
33	## this test and its recorder keep running while the game is paused:
34	## - this node's process_mode is ALWAYS (set in the scene). Its
35	##   _physics_process samples every physics tick, paused or not, and marks the
36	##   ticks on which the tree was paused, when nothing in the game ran;
37	## - it drives the scenarios with awaits on SceneTree's process_frame and
38	##   physics_frame signals, which the tree emits while paused;
39	## - Main is added under the tree's root, not under this node, so it inherits
40	##   the root's PAUSABLE mode as it does in the game. Under this node it would
41	##   inherit ALWAYS and never pause.
42	##
43	## Ticks. "st" counts from the tick a scenario's first key is read (st 0);
44	## setup ticks are negative. A swing tick counts the game ticks (ticks the tree
45	## was not paused) from the tick the press that starts the swing is read.
46	## At 30 fps a frame holds two ticks: slot a is the first, slot b the second. A
47	## key sent after a process_frame is read on the next frame's slot a. To have

## The edge test (CHANGE-BRIEF.md sections 6 and 9; step 5b). Run from the
## assignment folder:
##   scripts/run-test.sh test_rudy_edges.tscn 60
##   scripts/run-test.sh test_rudy_edges.tscn 30
##
## It works out how many physics ticks a rendered frame holds. With one (60
## fps) it runs E1-E7; with two (30 fps) it runs E1 and E2, once at each tick
## offset. Every edge is checked tick by tick, in physics ticks from the press.
##
## Rules this test keeps (the state test's, test_rudy_states.gd):
## - Each scenario starts a fresh real Main with the title skipped, as
##   checks.gd's _start_level() does (Main.title_shown = true before it is
##   instanced). E3's goblins and E6's pause need it.
## - Setup comes before a scenario's first key, and only then: it may place
##   Rudy at a spot on the level and lets him settle. From the first key on,
##   nothing writes his state, velocity, position, gear, hearts or mode. He
##   takes the sword by walking into the pickup.
## - Input is only InputEventKey events for the project's physical keys D, A,
##   Space, J and Esc, sent with Input.parse_input_event. A fresh press of a
##   key that is still held sends its key-up and key-down together, as the pin
##   does (test_rudy_pin.gd, step 5b).
## - It reads properties (Rudy's _slash_clock among them, read only), and
##   calls only read-only queries: is_on_floor(), get_children(), the
##   AnimationPlayer's current_animation and current_animation_position, and
##   Input's is_action_just_pressed()/is_action_just_released(). It never calls
##   play(), seek(), advance() or a state method.
## - This node is the recorder. Its process_physics_priority is 100, so on
##   every tick it samples after Rudy, his AnimationPlayer and the effects
##   driver: sample N is what tick N left.
##
## Pausing. Esc pauses the tree (Main.toggle_pause, from SystemKeys). So that
## this test and its recorder keep running while the game is paused:
## - this node's process_mode is ALWAYS (set in the scene). Its
##   _physics_process samples every physics tick, paused or not, and marks the
##   ticks on which the tree was paused, when nothing in the game ran;
## - it drives the scenarios with awaits on SceneTree's process_frame and
##   physics_frame signals, which the tree emits while paused;
## - Main is added under the tree's root, not under this node, so it inherits
##   the root's PAUSABLE mode as it does in the game. Under this node it would
##   inherit ALWAYS and never pause.
##
## Ticks. "st" counts from the tick a scenario's first key is read (st 0);
## setup ticks are negative. A swing tick counts the game ticks (ticks the tree
## was not paused) from the tick the press that starts the swing is read.
## At 30 fps a frame holds two ticks: slot a is the first, slot b the second. A
## key sent after a process_frame is read on the next frame's slot a. To have
## it read on slot b, the test awaits one physics_frame from a frame boundary,
## then sends the event and calls Input.flush_buffered_events() (the brief's
## second offset: one process_frame, then one physics_frame, then the event).
## Each swing's own press is read on slot a, so the edge presses read on slot
## a fall on its even swing ticks, and those on slot b on its odd ones.
##
## Prints a per-tick log, the scenarios, then the group EDGES, the ANOMALIES
## (the log lines around each failed check), and a RESULT line; quits 1 on any
## failure.

const MAIN_SCENE := preload("res://app/main.tscn")

const SETTLE_TICKS := 20 ## setup ticks after placing him, before the first key

- **Godot 4.7.2 stable** (`v4.7.2.stable.official.ed1daf0bf`, `logs/checks_60fps.log:1`). The project declares features `"4.7"` and the GL Compatibility renderer (`game/project.godot:16`).
- **60 physics ticks per second:** the project sets none, so the default holds.
- **Viewport** 1920 × 1080, `canvas_items` stretch, in a 1280 × 720 window (`game/project.godot:25-29`).
- Import before testing a fresh copy: `godot --headless --path game --import`.

## Tests: always through the wrapper

```bash
scripts/run-test.sh <test-file in game/tests/> <fps|realtime> [timeout-seconds]
```

- A `.tscn` test runs as the scene; a `.gd` test runs with `--script` and must `extends SceneTree`.
- A `--script` run cannot compile code that names an autoload such as `Sfx`, which `rudy.gd` does. Tests that load Rudy are scenes (`evidence/brief-probe/README.md`).
- The log is `logs/<test>_<fps>fps.log`. Exit 0 is not enough: the wrapper also fails on `SHADER ERROR`, `SCRIPT ERROR` and resource-load lines, because a scene with a missing texture loads and exits 0 (`evidence/load-error-probe/README.md`).
- Earlier tests and their counts, all 0 FAIL (`logs/`):
  - `checks.tscn`: 141 at 60;
  - `invulnerable_tint_checks.tscn`: 15 at 30, 60 and 144;
  - `test_slash_sparks_config.gd`: 108 checks;
  - `test_slash_sparks_state.tscn`: 14;
  - `test_run_dust_config.gd`: 61 checks;
  - `test_run_dust_state.tscn`: 14.
- New tests press keys with `Input.parse_input_event`, using the project's physical keys: D (move right), A (move left), Space (jump), J (slash). `checks.gd` uses `Input.action_press`; leave it as it is.
- Headless runs draw nothing. Frame strips need a Movie Maker run in a window.

## Godot 4 names (probed on 4.7.2: `evidence/brief-probe/README.md`)

- Write `loop_mode`, not `loop`. 4.7.2 happens to map `loop = true`, but Godot 4 code uses `loop_mode`.
- Write `speed_scale`, not `playback_speed`: `playback_speed` is dropped without a message.
- On `AnimatedSprite2D`, `sprite_frames` and `play()`, not `frames` and `playing = true`. `playing = true` does not play.
- `AnimationPlayer` and `AnimationTree` default to `callback_mode_process` idle (1); physics is 0 (Chapter 10; the probe confirmed it for `AnimationPlayer`).
- A track to a missing property prints nothing. If you are unsure a property exists in 4.7.2, check it (`ClassDB`, or load and read back) instead of guessing.

## Git

Git is read-only for the agent: `status`, `diff`, `log`, `show`. Do not commit, stage, stash, reset, switch branches or delete files with git; commits are mine.

I rewrote `CLAUDE.md`. It is now **105 lines**, and no other file changed. There's no `AGENTS.md`, so the file doesn't start with `@AGENTS.md`. I ran no tests: every count in the file comes from the existing `logs/`.

## What changed from the old CLAUDE.md, and why

- **Top line:** it now says a scoped Claude Code session drafted the file from `sessions/prompt-11.txt` on 2026-11-13, and that you review it. It also no longer says "where this file and the brief differ, the brief holds". Revision 5 withdraws Revision 2, so the brief is now imported, not just pointed to.
- **"Project context"** replaces "The project" and adds what this change needs, each with a file reference:
  - **Version and renderer:** Godot 4.7.2 stable, and the renderer from `project.godot:95-96`.
  - **State machine:** `rudy.gd` owns it. `_pick_clip()` hands a clip name to `RudyLook.play_clip()` every physics tick.
  - **The clips:** both sit on one player, `Look/AnimationPlayer`, set to the physics callback. `run` and `sword_run` play on `Look/Sprite` as a frame track. `slash` plays on the `Look/SlashRig` cutout rig, and its six track paths are listed.
  - **The library:** it is at `game/content/rudy/rudy_animations.tres` today, and Revision 5 moves it to `game/animations/`. That folder doesn't exist yet. The move must also update `test_rudy_clips.gd:43` and `test_rudy_states.gd:752`, which load the library by path.
  - **Scenes the clips appear in:** `rudy.tscn`, `main.tscn` and `test_rudy_pin.tscn`; the states and edges tests load `main.tscn` while they run.
  - **Previews:** the two existing previews hold only a frozen placeholder Rudy, not the clips. The previews Revision 5 names don't exist yet.
- **Tests:** the wrapper now has the `realtime` mode, how logs are named, the timeout, and the `couldn't resolve track` failure.
  - There is an exact command for every test, with its current count: clips 46, states 81, edges 98 at 60 and 66 at 30, and checks 141.
  - The pin's 19 checks are noted with T1, T2 and T6 failing on purpose.
  - Esc was added to the keys new tests may press, because the edge test uses it.
- **New sections:**
  - **"Current change"**, followed by exactly `@CHANGE-BRIEF.md`.
  - **"Ownership"**: every file in `game/shaders/` is yours and never edited by an agent, and clips are resources, never built in code at runtime. I also added that the wrapper stays as committed, because Revision 5 says so.
  - **"One authority"**: a table giving the single writer of each animated node and property, and saying who writes `Look` and the hitbox.
  - **"Out of scope"** and **"Unconfirmed"**.
- **"Godot 4 names"** now states the rule as you asked, including `AnimatedSprite` → `AnimatedSprite2D`. It also notes that no clip sets `Animation.step` yet.
- **Git** stays read-only, with `restore` and `clean` added to the forbidden list.

## What I could not confirm

1. **That `game/shaders/` is unchanged from Assignment 6.** Revision 5 says so, but this session wasn't allowed to run shell commands, so I couldn't run `git diff`.
2. **That `Animation.step` defaults to 1/30 s in 4.7.2.** Only Revision 5 says so; no probe in `evidence/` records it. All the file says for certain is that the library has no `step` lines.
3. **That the `realtime` mode works here.** There's no `*_realtime.log`, so no test has run that way in this folder. Its description comes only from the wrapper's code.
4. **Whether the read-back test breaks the "never built in code at runtime" rule.** Its negative checks make damaged copies of existing clips in memory (`test_rudy_clips.gd:34-38`). I read the rule as applying to game code, not tests; that's your call.
5. **The tint, sparks and dust counts** come from PASS lines in `logs/`, not from runs in this session. For the sparks config log, my search found 109 lines against the 108 checks recorded, which I didn't resolve.
